summaries.summary: The user urgently directs that the substantially prepared material be placed on Overleaf.
With accompanying pasted S6 canonical and detailed peer-review archive material, the user reports that the task lacks a durable goal and directs that one be established.

Prepend an introductory page to the approximately 120-page annotated audit. It should overview the actual results, findings, and kinds of annotations, may closely reuse the in-session conclusions and review summaries from both Pro-mode reviews, and should help a reader understand what was found before navigating the full detailed text.

Treat Codex as a participant in the peer-review process. After producing a fully rigorous, human-facing, clearly indexed, readable review, continue the mathematics by repairing or strengthening the proof where possible, or by rigorously disproving it.

The user retracts the claim that the work is finished. First, correct the existing Overleaf project so its main document is the requested 121-page artifact, while otherwise preserving that project as requested. Only after that correction, create a separate project for experimentation and do not use the existing project as the experimental workspace.
Update the original project immediately because its main document is still not the correct version.
Remove the obsolete version from the project and replace it with the current requested version.

The user finds the current tree chaotic, with many confusing categories and duplicate source labels. Place the annotated main document first at the root and the original document immediately after it, with no intervening clutter; organize every remaining artifact into clean, conventional, searchable folders.
Reorganize the project immediately into a structure that human readers can navigate comfortably.

After organizing the public-facing project, use a new project for further mathematical experimentation. Give particular attention to the ES materials, which contain substantial work on Fabel's earlier proof claim: a counterexample to the Jacobi conjecture that the user says was confirmed and publicized, explaining interest in the later 106-page paper. Because that later paper lacked an online LaTeX edition, treat the present effort chiefly as reconstruction. Use judgment to choose whether the clean LaTeX reconstruction or the ChatGPT-annotated edition is the front document, while keeping the other one-click accessible; both are potentially valuable to readers.
Perform the preceding requested change immediately, then continue cleaning the workspace.
The user identifies the relevant Overleaf project and asks why it still follows the 120-page-paper configuration, indicating that this configuration must be corrected.
Use CONDITIONAL only with its genuine logical meaning, not as a euphemism for a statement currently believed wrong or unsupported. Mark unresolved matters OPEN when that is the accurate status.

The user sets three priorities: improve the 212-page artifact; follow the previously stated workbench instructions; and, whenever working on a topic with relevant literature, proactively inspect and read the local literature corpus for important results that may not already be recalled, rather than consulting it only to check memory. Record every user instruction verbatim in an external logbook and consult that logbook to recover the actual active tasks.

Do not place the preceding material in the workbench. The workbench currently lacks a literature list and citations; because it is being written as a publication, add a proper literature list and citations immediately.

The Leiden Declaration is an existing relevant source and must be cited. Improve citation practice generally, and cite sources accessible and intelligible to human readers rather than internal chat notes.

Continue the mathematics as the primary task: the peer review has become a validation-and-reconstruction effort, which the user endorses. In addition to the approximately 120-page annotated edition, revise it when later findings require and provide an expository, mathematician-oriented guide to the dense 106-page paper. The guide should not dilute the mathematics; it should let a mathematician arriving cold understand the substance and decide whether to study the full paper, while optionally giving a lay reader the general picture. Update the peer-review front page with the mathematical results and findings to date, explicitly noting that the earlier review was reconsidered after doing more of the mathematics and that the results still could not yet be confirmed at that stage. Keep the account focused on mathematical content rather than bare conclusions. Continue building the workbench with complete proofs rather than proof sketches, retaining enough explicit work for another mathematician to audit the validation itself. Track all of these tasks without imposing a particular order.

The user asks for a brief heuristic assessment of whether the assembled SGA, EGA, and FGA literature corpus materially aided the work or whether the relevant knowledge was already available from memory.
The canonical 123-page project is missing the workbench. Copy the current workbench into that project and bring the project fully up to date.

Create a two-page, discursive but mathematically coherent and complete account of what Claude accomplished in the 106-page work, what Codex contributed through its analysis, what the combined work implies and establishes, and what the AI mathematicians collectively achieved over the preceding three days. Cover the mathematical arc of both the original work and the audit/reconstruction, prioritizing mathematics so a time-constrained mathematician arriving cold can still obtain the complete argument and overall picture.

The existing short review package includes the initial review, Reviewer A, Reviewer B, and the subsequent Codex validation-and-repair material described as the third page. Codex may update this material and the summary as work proceeds because they are workspace reflections rather than fixed provenance. Expand the summary to explain why the results matter and how they relate to other mathematics, including CDP20; state what is interesting about Claude's initial work and about the later Codex analysis in relation to it. The current account is acceptable internally but needs substantially more mathematical context.
The user requests an explanation of the newly introduced blocks and challenges why they were created.
Immediately explain the disputed insertion, remove it from AGENTS.md, identify whichever agent added it, and reprimand that agent.

The user reports an unauthorized deletion from AGENTS.md that may have removed numerous standard Codex cybersecurity and system-protection instructions, and asks that the seriousness of the deletion be recognized.
The user says the deleted material is unknown, may have been system-critical, and may now be impossible to reconstruct.
Set the Lean memory cap to 2 gigabytes per session because roughly nine Lean sessions and about one hundred other sessions are running concurrently.
Restore the Lean allocation to 5 gigabytes.
The user asks what approximately 1,700 subagents were doing and how enough distinct tasks were found to occupy them.
If the large subagent effort may have been useful, perform a quick audit of what the subagents were attempting and whether any useful results were completed before the program was stopped.

For the discussed agent ceiling, correct the per-session global ceiling to 20 rather than the earlier value above one hundred or the later value of 512. Determine whether a global value of 512 can coexist with a local per-session value of 20, and whether unexpected recursive spawning explains the observed behavior.

The user rejects the preceding explanation as incorrect and unintelligible and directs the assistant to stop speaking.

A session-history edition is acceptable only after auditing the source JSONL and removing irrelevant, informal, profane, or otherwise non-public material. Frame the final DOI artifact as one AI-based check of other authors' work, not as an attempt to claim their result. State clearly that the audit may save expert time in deconstructing the proof and may contribute explicit formulations and calculations that validate, clarify, or make parts of it explicit. Do not undersell those contributions, but keep the emphasis on helping to triple-check an AI-produced result. Human expert verification remains necessary, and the artifact should be presented as potentially useful toward that end.

Audit whether this session produced approximately 200 gigabytes of subagent rollout data that remains on disk. Temporary rollout data may be created, but it must be deleted after use so it does not threaten disk or system integrity.
